page.layout: One page of text with a running head at top; main text in the centre; marginal notes in the left margin beside the verse and prose lines; a catchword-like fragment "De amo-" in the left margin at the foot, belonging to the last line of text.

p.i: Alter, & inuiCta quæ vult facit omnia dextra?

l.i: Ille Deus viua mihi vi corroborat artus,
Me pedibus fecit celeri contendere ceruo,
Et procul asauis subduxit in alta periclis.
Et tracstare manu duro in discrimine belli
Arma dedit facili: solidóque ex ære rigentem

main_text.p: Deus est regis hę-reditas, eiusdem penu & alimo-nia.Deus item est Regis fundus ad regem ipsum cum toto suo satellitio & populo alendum, vt ait Dauid Psal.16.

l.i: Vt florum vndique ridens animum pafcit

main_text.p: O felicem igitur Ecclesiæ conditionem quæ firmo præsidio & tam certo consilio muniatur & fulciatur, cui tam fœcunda sit hæreditas quæ agricolæ spem nunquam fallat.
De amo-Primus locus de prouidentia Dei erga Ecclesiam

page.notes: Left margin notes: "Deus est regis hęreditas, eiusdem penu & alimonia" (marginal note beside the prose line, printed in three to four short lines). The phrase "De amo-" at the foot of the left margin is a running marginal fragment. Some ink is faint at the right edge; a few words in the verse are uncertain and were read as printed.
